LESSON: THE TREATY OF HUDAIBIYA

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: History of Islam
Topic 7.2: The Treaty of Hudaibiya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Treaty of Hudaibiya, part of History of Islam in Grade 6 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to resolve conflicts through peaceful means? 2. How can Muslims apply the lessons learnt from the treaty of Hudaibiya?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Treaty of Hudaibiya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: interacting with digital technology achieved as learners search and watch videos on the treaty of

Hudaibiya.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: Researching skill developed as learners draw lessons from the treaty of Hudaibiya

for application in life.

• Learning to Learn: learners develop relationships as they dramatise acts depicting peaceful ways of resolving conflicts.

Values:
Peace: care and compassion as learners dramatise acts depicting peaceful ways of resolving conflicts.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: Social cohesion as the treaty led to peaceful co-existence.

Link to other subjects:

Social Studies: conflict resolution mechanisms are covered.
